Spot Bitcoin ETFs Recorded $82.39 Million in Net Outflows, While Spot Ethereum ETFs Saw $69.68 Million in Net Outflows on October 16 (ET) On October 16 (ET), spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded total net outflows of $82.39 million, led by BlackRock's IBIT with $71.78 million in net outflows. Spot Ethereum ETFs recorded total net outflows of $69.68 million, marking their third consecutive day of net outflows, with all of the day's net outflows coming from BlackRock's ETHA. — link

Bitget's English Terms of Use, Marked as Updated Oct. 16, List Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan Among Prohibited Jurisdictions According to The Defiant, Bitget will discontinue services for certain users, with account-specific deadlines and withdrawal instructions sent directly to those affected. The exchange described it as a one-off exercise, said user funds remain safe, and noted that users who receive no notification can continue using their accounts under its terms. Its official support account also cited the prohibited-jurisdiction list when responding to restrictions on Russian users. One affected user reported an Oct. 21 deadline, but Bitget's main announcement gave no common deadline, affected account count or specific regulatory basis. — link

On-Chain Data Shows Increasing Number of Hackers Moving Stolen Funds to Zcash for Laundering On-chain analyst Specter noted that following ZachXBT's disclosure regarding the Bitget exploiter shielding stolen assets via Zcash (ZEC), multiple other threat actors have begun channeling stolen proceeds into ZEC. These flows include illicit funds traced from the Cryptobills Ledger security incident and the $12 million Triple-A exploit, signaling that attackers are actively leveraging Zcash's privacy features for money laundering and obfuscation. — link

BIS: Stablecoins and Bank Deposits Act as Substitutes as Deposit Hikes Slow Stablecoin Growth BIS (Bank for International Settlements) working paper finds that stablecoins and bank deposits act as direct portfolio substitutes. Analyzing U.S. data, the authors show that a 1-basis-point hike in bank deposit rates cuts 10-week stablecoin market cap growth by roughly 3 percentage points (and up to ~9 percentage points under an IV approach). The substitution effect is significantly stronger for onshore-tied USDC (-4.8%) than offshore-centric USDT (-1.9%) and holds across bank CD rates and DeFi lending yields, demonstrating that traditional bank deposit pricing exerts an active drag on stablecoin growth. — link
